coordinates: Native 2144 by 1424, origin at the upper left. The house with the remaining green number 3 plaque is used. u increases to the right, v down.

left_gable.visible_window_jamb_rails: Several narrow white vertical bars and two raised central stiles. A warm red reveal borders the pale outer casing. Pattern behind the glass is an interior curtain and is not a decorative glazing bar.
left_gable.left_front_glass_temporal: Four vertical light intervals are represented as bounded glazed divisions. Lower lock and handles are below reliable resolution.

pale_verge_native_color_samples.inspection: Pale band sampled from the high-resolution original red/green/blue values; points above the beige edge at (707,145) and (736,159) are sky, while (765,171) is the roof behind the bargeboard.

right_hip.visible_clear_front_leaves: The left reddish casement stands out into the open dark recess. The more frontal leaf has two intermediate horizontal rails and three clear glazed lights. Objects seen through the opening and the fittings have insufficient geometric evidence.
right_hip.end_condition: Joins the taller neighbour on the source image right; use a flush end closure only at the visible boundary.

main_roof.foreground_streams: Separate dark inclined lengths in front of the roof look like rods or conductors. Their directions differ and none is used as a structural cheek edge.

plan_depth.method: Within a single planar pitch, the cross ratio along the projected drainage direction gives the fraction of eave-to-ridge depth. The inferred slope vanishing point is uncertain: a 4-of-16 fit is only a sensitivity example. The final roof fit supplies the common surface.
plan_depth.recessed_back: The unseen rear wall is left at the roof intersection, with rear depth approximate.

independent_reference.use: The paired composition of gabled and transverse-eaved roof windows is also visible on the section bearing numbers 1 and 2. Sash colours, rails, later metal rack and casement positions on that section are not transferred to number 3.

roof_assembly_by_two_cameras.fabric: The diagonal on the little right dormer roof is an eight-piece overlapping terracotta coping with a pale cheek visible under its edge. Rows of clay tile are visible below the cheek. Its rear end is hidden in the lower street view.

working_dimensions_relative_to_white_mid.right_coping_tail_visibility_constraint: With P1 held at (997,130), a tail at Y=2.0 m would stand about 3.5 px above the present street photograph’s eave silhouette at (323.9,35.5). Y=2.5 m falls 1.2 px below it and the model Y=3.075 m falls 6.2 px below it. This constrains a lower bound, not its precise rear location. Six visible tile laps near the neighbour give a depth estimate independent of the hidden ridge endpoint.

roof_assembly_by_two_cameras.uncertainty: The street eave hides the lower jambs and flashing in the 640 × 432 view. The inner sash depth and clay courses are estimated. Second-photo fixed pale stile point (222,65) falls on glazing in the current projection outside the two-pixel allowance.
